attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed Substack post, not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: Calling the idea 'bonkers' is an unhedged dismissal, so it reads as a firm expectation that no perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots would exist within a year. The threshold 'perfectly' and the one-year horizon are both preserved. The text has no may/might hedge.

contract.note: The literal reading of 'perfectly reliable, hallucination-free' comes from the speaker's own words. Reading the horizon as about 23 Feb 2025 is reasonable. The support condition, a measurable hallucination rate in leading chatbots, fairly tracks the claim.

evidence.note: This is an independent leaderboard dated 28 Feb 2025, five days after the horizon, which fits 'around February 2025'. Every listed leading model (Gemini, GPT-4o, o1 and others) hallucinated above zero, and the best scored 0.7%. It covers summarization only, but any hallucination is enough to show a model is not hallucination-free.

output.rationale: The forecast was that no perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbot would exist by about Feb 2025, and that horizon has passed. Vectara's independent measurement from 28 Feb 2025 shows every leading model still hallucinating at a measurable rate, which meets the support condition. Nothing in the packet shows a model with zero hallucinations. The benchmark's scope (document summarization) is a limit, but it does not undercut the result, because the claim required perfection.
